Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board (Board) on any matter listed on the

the Oral Communications period.

Board Member Apodaca called the special meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Norwalk
City Hall, Council Chambers. Responding to roll call were Board Member Apodaca,
Board Member Vernola-Salas, and Vice Chair Barragan. Board Member Macias and
Chair Lopez were absent. Also present were Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of
Community Development; Gabriela Garcia, Senior Management Analyst; Carlos Rojas,
Senior Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

REORGANIZATION OF THE BOARD

By unanimous voice vote, Board Member Apodaca was appointed to serve as Chair, and
Board Member Vernola-Salas was appointed to serve as Vice Chair for the upcoming
year.

MEETING MINUTES

The Board approved the minutes of the Special Property Maintenance and Building
Rehabilitation Appeals Board Meeting of June 26, 2024.

REPORT OF DELINQUENT TRASH COLLECTION ACCOUNTS

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Gabriela Garcia, Senior
Management Analyst presented a report stating that the City of Norwalk provides
mandatory refuse service to protect the public health and welfare of its residents; that, as
such, Athens Services picks up trash weekly billing customers on a quarterly basis; that
payment for services is due within thirty (30) days from the billing date; that a late fee of
$25.00 is added if payment has not been made by the end of the service quarter; that the
hauler makes attempts during the year to collect on past-due accounts; and that as
authorized in the Municipal Code, the hauler is allowed to seek payment through the tax
rolls in July of each year for the period of May 1st of the previous year through April 30th
of the current year;

Further, Ms. Garcia shared that in May of this year, 2,122 notices were prepared and
mailed to all property owners with a delinquent balance as of April 30, 2025; that the
delinquent amounts totaled $396,923; that as of June 4, 2025, there were 907 accounts
that have not settled their account, with a combined balance of $231,694.90; that
payments will continue to be received until July 31st; and that staff recommends that the
Board forward the listed properties to City Council with a recommendation that the
delinquent properties be placed on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding balance
is paid prior to July 31st, 2025.

SUBJECT: PUBLIC HEARING – REPORT OF DELINQUENT TRASH COLLECTION
  ACCOUNTS

Background:

Norwalk Municipal Code Section 8.48.280, Mandatory Service, requires all solid waste collected
from residential, commercial, or industrial premises for a fee, service charge, or other
consideration, shall be collected by a solid waste enterprise under the provisions of an exclusive
contract awarded by City Council.

City procedures state that any owner who has a delinquent account as of May 1, 2026 which
covers the period of May 1, 2025 to April 30, 2026 shall be sent, by mail, written notification that
the Appeals Board will review all such delinquent accounts during a public hearing. On May 1,
2026, Athens Services, the City’s solid waste hauler, mailed 1,438 notices that sought a
combined amount of $353,655.48. As of June 10, 2026, there are 1,008 accounts that have not
settled their account, with a combined balance of $260,166.38.

Daily payments and/or adjustments are being processed and will continue through July 31, 2026.
A City administrative fee of $25 will be added to each delinquent account not paid by July 31,
2026.

Fiscal Impact:

The City will be reimbursed $25 for each account on the final lien list for administrative costs.
The total amount will not be known until the final list is complete on July 31, 2026.

Citizens Advised:

Notices were mailed to all delinquent account holders by May 1, 2026, and posted at the City’s
three designated places and published in The Norwalk Patriot on May 29, 2026.
